sections.html:
Two Somerset offices split the work. The Property Valuation Administrator, or PVA, sets a value on each parcel and answers at (606) 679-1812. The Pulaski County Sheriff's tax office prints the bill and collects it. Staff are there weekdays from 8:00 AM until 4:00 PM, and questions can go to taxes@pulaskisheriff.com.

Neither office votes on rates. Each taxing district sets its own levy, from the fiscal court to the school board. Three public school systems serve the county: Pulaski County, Somerset Independent and Science Hill Independent. Which one covers your house changes the school share of the bill.

The sheriff bills more than houses. The same office collects on real estate with school taxes, tangible property, franchise and gas taxes, undeveloped land, oil, and limestone, sand and gravel. If you own more than one kind of property, ask whether each has its own bill.

Bills begin to be mailed in early October. The sheriff's steps look like this, and the 5 percent January charge matches KRS 134.015.

Pulaski County sheriff: amount owed by payment date
When paidAmount
October 1 to November 1Bill less a 2 percent discount
November 2 to December 31Base amount
January 1 to January 31Base amount plus 5 percent
February 1 to April 15Base amount plus 21 percent
April 16 onwardPay the County Clerk, (606) 679-2042

At the counter you can pay with cash, check or card, and cards carry a small added fee. Part payments are refused, so bring the whole amount. To pay by mail, enclose a stamped return envelope and the office sends back a receipt with your check. A lost bill is replaced at no charge.

Somerset is the county seat, with Burnside, Eubank, Ferguson and Science Hill also in the county. The July 2025 population estimate is 67,384, up 3.6 percent from 2020. There are 26,210 households, and owners live in 72.5 percent of homes. A typical home is valued at $166,900 and typical gross rent is $803. Builders pulled 129 permits in 2025, so most buyers are choosing among existing houses.

Lake Cumberland and its houseboat trade in the south shape part of the market. US 27 runs north and south, Kentucky 80 east and west, and Interstate 75 is about 28 miles east. Lexington is 76 miles north. A house with roof, septic or shoreline trouble can go to a direct cash buyer, with any tax owed settled at closing.

sections.h2: Homestead exemption and the state rate
sections.html:
Kentucky's state rate for 2025 is 10.6 cents on every hundred dollars of assessment. Local districts stack their own rates on top, so the sheriff's bill for your address shows the full total.

Owners who are 65 or older, or totally disabled, can take a deduction from the assessed value. The amount is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026. Apply at the PVA at (606) 679-1812, and confirm the current figure there, since the state revises it.

Paying inside the October 1 to November 1 window earns the 2 percent discount on the whole bill, which is worth planning for if you are still the owner of record that fall.

Every Kentucky appeal opens with a meeting at the PVA office, whether the parcel is a Lake Cumberland cottage or a farm near Eubank. The roll can be inspected for thirteen days from May's first Monday. At the meeting the PVA must explain how the number was reached and record your claimed value, anything agreed and the result.

  • The appeal reaches the clerk on the first workday after the roll closes.
  • A local board of property owners hears cases about a month later, in a session of up to five days.
  • Supporting papers are required: land and building descriptions, insurance policies, construction cost and sales listings. A file without them is rejected.
  • Anyone you hire to speak for you must come from the statutory list and hold your signed authorization.

If bills print before the board rules and the final value is higher than your claim, a supplemental bill follows for the difference.

sections.h2: Who owes the tax when a house sells mid year?
sections.html:
Whoever held the parcel at the start of the year owes the fall bill, though a closing may prorate it. Your closing attorney can explain how the contract divides the year, and the tax office can tell you whether the parcel shows paid or open.

Under KRS 134.015 the tax is the owner's personal debt as of the assessment date, and a lien described in KRS 134.420 stays on the land for eleven years. Lenders that escrow often pay the bills they hold. The bill is still the homeowner's duty, so give your lender a copy if your mailing address changed.

A seller moving away should also tell the PVA. The older owner deduction follows the person, so the buyer has to apply on their own.

On April 16 the sheriff passes unpaid bills to the County Clerk. Each one becomes a certificate of delinquency backed by a lien. A buyer of a delinquent bill collects the tax plus 12 percent a year and costs such as attorney and filing fees. The house itself is not auctioned at that stage.

The clerk adds interest of 1 percent monthly, and the county attorney's commission and postage are added after notices go out. Notices go out before a sale, which the law places between 90 and 135 days after transfer. Paying the clerk before the sale day keeps an investor from acquiring the bill.

Unpaid tax does not block a sale, but it has to be cleared at closing. The steps are simple.

  • Ask the sheriff, or the County Clerk after April 15, for a written payoff on every open year.
  • Give that figure to the closing attorney, who deducts it from your proceeds.
  • If an investor has already bought the bill, get the payoff from that holder instead, with interest and costs included.
  • Check the title for a lien before you sign a contract, since the lien stays with the land through a sale.

A cash sale of a house in rough shape follows the same path. The buyer skips repairs and lender approval, and the tax owed is paid out of the sale money at the table. Bring your latest bill, your deed and a photo ID to the closing office so nothing slows the day.

faqs.q: Can I pay a Pulaski County tax bill by card?
faqs.a: Yes, at the counter of the sheriff's tax office, with a small fee added for cards. Cash and checks work too, but the full bill must be paid at once because part payments are refused.

faqs.q: What are the extra charges after January in Pulaski County?
faqs.a: The sheriff adds 5 percent for January and 21 percent for February 1 through April 15. After that the County Clerk takes payment.

faqs.q: When does the Pulaski County early discount apply?
faqs.a: From October 1 through November 1, a 2 percent discount comes off the bill. The base amount is due November 2 through December 31.

faqs.q: Where do I claim the older owner deduction in Pulaski County?
faqs.a: Call the PVA at (606) 679-1812. The deduction is $49,100 for owners 65 and up or totally disabled, for 2025 and 2026.

faqs.q: Will the sheriff auction my house over unpaid Pulaski County tax?
faqs.a: Not at the sheriff stage. After April 15 the bill goes to the County Clerk and can be sold to an investor, who then holds a lien with 12 percent yearly interest and costs.
